title: Reserve Talent Pool Activation Cookbook — 21-day rapid coverage plan
body:
Purpose
This working doc describes a compact, repeatable protocol to activate a small ‘reserve talent pool’ and onboard short-term replacements (or accelerated hires) in 21 calendar days. It’s designed for roles that must be kept staffed with minimal service disruption: on-call SREs, runtime infra engineers, customer implementation leads, and core platform product engineers.

Scope and assumptions
- Scope: roles classified Priority A / mission-critical in the hiring matrix.
- Assumes a standing reserve pool (scorecarded and consented) of 20–50 pre-screened candidates maintained by People Ops + Staffing team.
- Activation target: candidate in seat (full access & first week shadowing) within 21 days of trigger.
- Not a replacement for full requisition hiring; this is contingency coverage and rapid stabilization.

Activation triggers (examples)
1) Unplanned departure of an on-call rotation member with fewer than 6 team-week overlaps to backfill.
2) Unexpected sustained throughput loss where headcount gap increases incident risk.
3) Regulatory or client requirement to maintain a certified staff count.

Pool segmentation & readiness taxonomy
- Tier 1 (Hot): cleared, score >= 85, 100% available for start in 7–14 days, has standard NDAs and KBA verified.
- Tier 2 (Warm): score 70–84, available for 14–30 days, requires targeted upskilling (1–2 focused modules).
- Tier 3 (Cold): score < 70 or expired checks — used only as last resort and requires full hire cycle.

Scorecard snapshot (how we pre-evaluate)
- Core skills (coding/data/infra): 40 pts.
- System design & incident reasoning: 20 pts.
- Communication (async + stakeholder): 15 pts.
- Cultural fit / role commitment: 15 pts.
- Eligibility checks (work auth, NDAs, background): 10 pts.
- Minimum pass for pool membership: 70/100.

Activation playbook (day-by-day summary)
Days 0–2: Triage + candidate selection - Incident owner & hiring partner confirm role scope and scope-reduction (if any).
- People Ops run the reserve filter (Tier 1 first) and return 3 candidates within 48 hours.
- Interview owner: team lead or rotation manager schedules 30–45m focused interview within 48 hours.

Days 3–7: Decision loop & offer sprint
- Day 3–4: On-the-hour interview scorecards completed by panel (use condensed rubric below).
- Day 4–5: Compensation anchor & offer packet prepared by Recruiting Ops. Offer should include a 90-day review and clear ramp expectations.
- Day 6–7: Candidate acceptance window; at-offer must include start date options and an accelerated onboarding calendar.

Days 8–14: Access, micro-onboarding, shadowing
- IT & security perform accelerated provisioning (VPN, SSO, pager access) within 72 hrs of confirmed start date.
- Assign buddy and first-week shadow schedule; curated incident runbook snapshot provided.
- Mini-training modules (recorded): platform basics, common runbook playbooks, top 10 pager incidents and escalation matrix.

Days 15–21: Ownership handoff & monitored transition
- Gradual responsibility handoff: candidate takes first low-risk pager rotation under mentor observation.
- Daily check-ins with hiring owner for first 7 business days.
- 21-day stabilization retro to flag outstanding skill gaps and decide on permanent requisition escalation.

Condensed interview rubric (45m rapid loop)
- Kickoff / calibration (5m): role context given by hiring manager.
- Tech probe (20m): focused coding/system design problem that reflects the 3 highest-risk on-call incidents for the team. Evaluate for correctness, debug approach, and trade-off reasoning.
- Incident reasoning (10m): present a short past incident and ask candidate to run an RCA-lite and propose immediate mitigations.
- Communication & fit (5m): stakeholder comms and working style.
- Scoring matrix: technical 50, incident reasoning 25, communication 15, availability/commitment 10. Pass = 70+.

Offer packaging guidance
- Short-term contingency hires should include: explicit phrase about 90-day review, transparent path to full requisition (if appropriate), prorated benefits note, and clear performance objectives for day 7, day 21, and day 90.

Onboarding templates and artifacts
- Week-0 checklist (pre-start): equipment ship date, SSO invite, NDA & I-9 check completed, pager & rotation calendar.
- Day-1 agenda: team intro, runbook tour, access verification, first shadow slot.
- Week-1 agenda: low-risk tickets, paired incidents, documentation assignments.

Communication artifacts (copy-paste templates)
1) Internal activation Slack (to #eng-ops or relevant rotation):
"Heads-up: activating Reserve Pool for [ROLE] due to [TRIGGER]. Candidates recommended: [A,B,C]. Hiring partner: @Name. Expect first shadow start: [DATE]. Please prioritize provisioning tickets: IT-12345, SEC-678"

2) Candidate outreach email brief:
"Hi [Name], we have a short-term immediate opportunity at Redwood Inference on the [team]. Role is a 90-day accelerated coverage with potential conversion. Are you available to interview in the next 48 hours? If yes, please share earliest possible start date. — Asha, People Ops"

Fail-safe & escalation matrix
- If no Tier 1 candidate available within 7 days, expand to Tier 2 and run 48-hour targeted upskill module.
- If offer declined by final candidate, escalate to Staffing Head for discretionary increased comp band.
- If provisioning delays exceed 72 hours post-start, SRE lead to request emergency admin escalation through Security & IT.

Risk register (short list)
- Risk: Candidate burnout / attrition after temporary placement. Mitigation: include explicit retention bonus and clear path to conversion.
- Risk: Incomplete provisioning leads to reduced coverage. Mitigation: pre-approved emergency tickets and a shadowing-only plan.
- Risk: Quality gap vs permanent hire. Mitigation: pair with mentor, limit critical duties until day 21 review.

Metrics to monitor for each activation
- Time-to-first-available-candidate (hrs).
- Offer-acceptance window (days).
- Time-to-provision (hrs).
- Incidents handled by temporary hire vs mentor intervention rate (first 21 days).
- Conversion-to-perm rate within 90 days.

Role owner responsibilities (quick list)
- Hiring manager: define reduced-scope responsibilities and shadow schedule.
- People Ops (Activation lead): select candidates, coordinate interviews, run offer sprint.
- Staffing: comp calibration and rapid offer.
- IT/Sec: provisioning and access SLA enforcement.

Operational notes & next steps
- This doc is a living playbook. People Ops should run a quarterly tabletop activation drill with one Priority A team to validate timings and identify bottlenecks.
- Action items: 1) Create a standard reserve-pool consent form for candidates. 2) Automate Tier 1 filter in ATS and surface top 5 weekly. 3) Build a 21-day activation dashboard (KPI tiles above).

Appendix: quick checklists (copy-ready)
Pre-start (to be completed before day 0): Equipment ordered, SSO invite sent, NDA + eligibility confirmed, Manager kickoff scheduled.
Day-1 (copy-ready): 09:00 intro + runbook, 10:30 access verification, 13:00 first shadow slot, 17:00 end-of-day check-in.
21-day retro template (questions): Did candidate meet the 21-day objectives? Outstanding training items? Recommendation: Extend/convert/replace?

Notes to reviewers
- This doc borrows some language from existing onboarding artifacts but focuses on the contingency playbook and reduced-scope rapid ramp. Looking for feedback from SRE leads and Staffing on timing feasibility and any legal/benefits constraints for accelerated offers.
